title: Node provisioning command trace & hypotheses
content:
Context:
- Trying to repro intermittent node join failures on new GCE nodes created by terraform + cloud-init + kubeadm. Failures mostly seen in eu-west region, spots of higher preemptions.
- Symptoms: node never transitions to Ready. kubeadm join succeeds (reports success), but kubelet stays CrashLoopBackOff or repeatedly dies on first boot.
- This note is a chronological command trace, outputs, and my hypotheses. Use as breadcrumbs for follow-ups.

Commands tried (raw):
1) journalctl -u kubelet -b --no-pager | tail -n 120 \   >>> output snippet:
Feb 14 07:11:22 vm-123 systemd[1]: Started kubelet: The Kubernetes Node Agent.
Feb 14 07:11:23 vm-123 kubelet[1125]: E0214 07:11:23.123456   1125 server.go:240] failed to run Kubelet: failed to create kubelet config: open /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml: permission denied
Feb 14 07:11:23 vm-123 systemd[1]: kubelet.service: Main process exited, code=exited, status=1/FAILURE

2) sudo ls -la /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml && sudo stat -c '%U:%G %a' /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml \   >>> output:
-rw-r----- 1 root root 456 Mar 10 07:09 /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml
root:root 640

Observation: kubelet running as rootless? or expects kubelet:kubelet ownership. Config ends up root:root due to cloud-init templating + umask.

3) grep -i error /var/log/cloud-init-output.log | tail -n 40 \   >>> output snippets show cloud-init failing to chown certain files, intermittent network timeouts fetching apt packages, and a failed systemctl enable kubelet: 
cloud-init[501]: Failed to enable service kubelet: Unit file kubelet.service does not exist.

Hypothesis: Our cloud-init script sometimes races: kubeadm/kubelet packages not fully installed before we attempt to enable kubelet or write config files. That leaves config owned by root and kubelet service not configured correctly.

4) kubeadm join ... --v=5  (re-run with verbose) \   >>> observed:
[preflight] Running pre-flight checks
[preflight] Some fatal errors occurred:
        [ERROR Swap]: running with swap on is not supported. Please disable swap

Note: swap present on image. Our base image has swapfile created by default (fstrim + zram). Need to ensure cloud-init disables swap before kubeadm join. Strange that some nodes proceed while others fail — maybe swap disable step is conditional.

5) systemctl status containerd.service && journalctl -u containerd -b --no-pager | tail -n 80 \   >>> output:
Feb 14 07:12:00 vm-123 containerd[950]: time="2026-02-14T07:12:00Z" level=error msg="failed to load plugin io.containerd.grpc.v1.cri: io: read/write on closed pipe"
containerd.service - container runtime
   Loaded: loaded (/lib/systemd/system/containerd.service; enabled; vendor preset: enabled)
   Active: active (running) since Feb 14 07:11:50; 15s ago

But there are intermittent "failed to load plugin" errors in log at start. Could be caused by older config or leftover /var/lib/containerd state from previous instance.

6) lsblk && grep -i nvme /var/log/dmesg | tail -n 60 \   >>> There are some NVMe attach/detach messages immediately after boot which line up with kubelet errors about rootfs permissions. Some nodes showed: "nvme 1:0:0: device has been removed" — indicates cloud provider attaching block devices late. If kubelet sees transient disk removal, it might mark disk pressure or fail volume plugin initialization.

7) kubectl get nodes (from control plane) -> node shows NotReady with conditions: KubeletNotReady, OutOfDisk, NetworkUnavailable on some attempts. kubectl describe node vm-123 shows:
  Conditions:
    Type             Status  Reason                Message
    ----             ------  ------                -------
    KubeletReady     False   KubeletCrash         kubelet has crashed: exit code 1
    OutOfDisk        True    KubeletHasDiskPressure  kubelet detected disk pressure

Notes: DiskPressure while system disk is only 30% used. Indicates ephemeral mountpoint (e.g., /var/lib/kubelet) not writable or remounted read-only due to fs errors.

Commands executed to remediate (ad-hoc):
- sudo chown -R kube:kube /var/lib/kubelet || sudo chown -R root:kubelet /var/lib/kubelet (results varied). On nodes where chown fixed ownership, kubelet started.
- sudo swapoff -a; systemctl mask dphys-swapfile.service 
- sudo systemctl restart containerd && journalctl -u containerd -f (sometimes containerd recovered)
- sudo rm -rf /var/lib/containerd/io.containerd.snapshotter.v1.*/mounts/* (risky; used only in ephemeral lab nodes)

Additional troubleshooting commands and outputs saved here (snippets):
- kubectl logs -n kube-system kube-proxy-abc --previous -> shows iptables init failing due to missing xt_conntrack module on some images.
- dmesg | tail -> "overlayfs: upper fs has no space" observed once when image overlay not cleaned after previous preempt/restore.

Hypotheses summary (ranked):
1) Race in cloud-init: packages + systemd units not fully installed/enabled before kubeadm/kubelet steps run. Leads to missing unit, wrong file ownership, or kubelet starting with partial config. (High confidence)
2) Block device re-attach timing (NVMe/detach) on GCE preemptible nodes causing /var mounts to be remounted or device to be late => kubelet disk pressure or containerd plugin initialization fails. (Medium confidence)
3) Swap not reliably disabled by image; kubeadm preflight fails on some nodes causing manual intervention. (Medium confidence)
4) Stale containerd state from image snapshot causing plugin load errors on cold boot. (Low-Med confidence)
5) Helm/Daemonset interactions: we have a bootstrapping DaemonSet (sysctl/iptables) that runs early; if it sets iptables modules and fails, network condition becomes "NetworkUnavailable" and CNI doesn't reconcile. (Low confidence)

Immediate next steps / tasks to validate (TODOs):
- Add explicit "systemctl daemon-reload" and ensure kubelet.service exists before enabling in cloud-init. Add loop with sleep+check to fail-fast if missing.
- Ensure cloud-init disables swap early in boot (before kubeadm join). Add `swapoff -a` to head of user-data and remove any fstrim/zram setup that recreates swap.
- Modify terraform instance template to wait for stable NVMe attachments: use a small script that retries `lsblk` until expected disks present before kubeadm join.
- Bake image that cleans /var/lib/containerd on first boot or uses unique runtime dirs per instance to avoid leftover snapshot state.
- Add probe script to SRE bootstrap that checks ownership of /var/lib/kubelet and fixes before systemctl start kubelet.

Useful one-liners to reproduce/collect on a failing node:
- sudo journalctl -u kubelet -b --no-pager | sed -n '1,200p' > /tmp/kubelet-logs.txt\- sudo tar -czf /tmp/node-debug-$(hostname)-$(date +%Y%m%d).tgz /var/log /var/lib/containerd /var/lib/kubelet /etc/kubernetes /var/log/cloud-init-output.log\- sudo showmount -e (if NFS used)

Notes to self:
- When filing JIRA, include the node debug tarball, cloud-init user-data, and the specific image/AMI id.
- Re-run repro using fresh preemptible instance in the lab with STRACE on kubelet start if timing issues persist.
- Coordinate with infra-images team: ask whether any changes were made to containerd config or cloud-init templates in the last two weeks (linked PR above).

Slack snippets to include in ticket:
- "Observed kubelet failing with permission denied opening /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml. Fixing ownership restored kubelet on 3/7 attempts. Suspect cloud-init race."
- "NVMe attach/detach messages in dmesg line up exactly with containerd plugin startup errors — possible race before mount complete."

This doc is intentionally messy. Use as a starting trace to build a reproducible test and a short postmortem. Save any new logs to the JIRA ticket JIRA-INFRA-887 and ping Jonah for infra-image follow-up.
